title: [...] and [...] Headings
summary: Relationships between topics are normally expressed by heading-subdivision combinations (--Effect of [...] on, --[...] influences, --Psychological aspects, --Social aspects). A [Topic A] and [Topic B] heading is established only when a work discusses the relationship between two very general topics broadly and from both perspectives. Order of A and B follows precedent. References: 450 from the reversed form, 550 to Topic B (or its established equivalent). Existing conflicting headings are kept. Religion relationships follow H 1998.
validation_rules: A heading of the form `[Topic A] and [Topic B]` expressing a relationship between two topics is valid only if individually established in the authority file; it is not constructible ad hoc. (H 310 sec. 1)

Prefer a heading-subdivision construction (`--Effect of [...] on`, `--[...] influences`, `--Psychological aspects`, `--Social aspects`, etc.) over an unestablished `[Topic A] and [Topic B]` heading when the relationship is viewed from the perspective of one main topic. (H 310 Background, sec. 1)
Examples of valid "and" relationship headings: `Education and crime`, `Feminism and the arts`, `Government and the press`, `Agriculture and energy`. (H 310 sec. 1, sec. 2)

Invalid "and" headings and their correct forms: `Drugs and body temperature` -> `Body temperature--Effect of drugs on`; `English literature and Italian civilization` -> `English literature--Italian influences`; `Mass media and society` -> `Mass media--Social aspects`; `Psychology and advertising` -> `Advertising--Psychological aspects`. (H 310 sec. 1)

The order of Topic A and Topic B follows precedent in existing headings; the reversed form (e.g. `Arts and feminism`, `Energy and agriculture`) is a UF reference, not a valid heading. (H 310 sec. 1, sec. 2)
Do not use an "and" heading for a work that discusses two topics distinctly; assign separate headings for each topic instead. (H 310 sec. 1)

Some "and" headings represent two topics normally treated together (e.g. `Bolts and nuts`) or add terms for clarification (e.g. `Files and rasps`); these are valid as established and are not relationship headings. (H 310 Background note)
For relationships between a topic and religion, or a specific religion or denomination, consult H 1998 rather than constructing `[Topic] and [religion]`. (H 310 Background)
Existing established "and" headings that conflict with these instructions remain valid and continue to be used. (H 310 sec. 3)

sections.heading: 1. Proposing new headings.
sections.text:
Establish new headings in the form [Topic A] and [Topic B] only when the work being cataloged discusses the relationship between the topics from both perspectives and in such broad terms that it could not accurately be described by the use of a main heading and subdivision.

Examples of appropriate [Topic A] and [Topic B] headings:

```
150 ## $a Education and crime
150 ## $a Feminism and the arts
150 ## $a Government and the press
```

Examples of inappropriate [Topic A] and [Topic B] headings:

```
150 ## $a Drugs and body temperature
 use instead: 650 #0 $a Body temperature $x Effect of drugs on.

150 ## $a English literature and Italian civilization
 use instead: 650 #0 $a English literature $x Italian influences.

150 ## $a Mass media and society
 use instead: 650 #0 $a Mass media $x Social aspects.

150 ## $a Psychology and advertising
 use instead: 650 #0 $a Advertising $x Psychological aspects.
```

Do not propose headings of this type for works that discuss two topics distinctly, rather than the relationship between them. For such works, assign as many individual headings as are required to bring out the topics discussed.

Decide which topic to give as Topic A and which as Topic B based on precedents in existing headings in the subject authority file.

sections.heading: 2. References.
sections.text: Add the following reference fields whenever proposing a new [Topic A] and [Topic B] heading:

sections.heading: a. If [Topic B] is an established heading:
sections.text:
```
450 ## $a [Topic B] and [Topic A]
550 ## $w g $a [Topic B]
```

Example:

```
150 ## $a Feminism and the arts
450 ## $a Arts and feminism
550 ## $w g $a Arts
```

sections.heading: b. If [Topic B] is not an established heading:
sections.text:
```
450 ## $a [Topic B] and [Topic A]
550 ## $w g $a [established heading representing the concept of Topic B]
```

Example:

```
150 ## $a Agriculture and energy
450 ## $a Energy and agriculture
550 ## $w g $a Power resources
```

sections.heading: 3. Using existing headings.
sections.text: Make no attempt to change existing headings in the subject authority file that conflict with these instructions. Continue to use such headings for new works being cataloged.
